workup.reason_code_summary: The issuer alleges the cardholder was charged £54.00 twice on 12 April 2025 by Roastline Coffee Co for a single purchase. To defend, the merchant must prove all three of the following: the two charges were for two separate purchases, each purchase event is documented, and each charge has its own timestamp and authorisation code.

requirements.reasoning: The two invoices carry different order IDs and entirely different baskets: coffee beans in order A and brewing equipment in order B. The £54.00 totals match only because order A received a £6.00 loyalty discount. The merchant's own note saying 'Both charges are valid' is an assertion and carries no weight beyond the underlying order data.

Each purchase has its own invoice number. Each also has a separate DPD consignment number and delivery date. The delivery lines are merchant-recorded rather than carrier proof-of-delivery, but separate invoices meet the documentation requirement on their own.

Each charge has a distinct authorisation code (442189 and 552781). The capture timestamps are about 11.5 hours apart. The disputed transaction's clock time of 08:11:33 matches order A, although the timezone label differs from the transaction record (see caveats).

workup.action_justification: All three requirements are satisfied: two distinct orders with different order IDs, items, invoices, consignments and authorisation codes.
workup.rationale: The cardholder was charged twice on 12 April 2025 for two separate orders, not one transaction processed twice. Order RL-ORDER-44188 (invoice RL-88291) covered coffee beans and was authorised under code 442189 at 08:11. Order RL-ORDER-44192 (invoice RL-88294) covered an Aeropress Go kit and filter papers and was authorised under code 552781 at 19:42. The two orders were dispatched in separate DPD consignments (7711224488 and 7711224501) to the cardholder's billing address, 14 Branston Road, London N1 4PD. The identical £54.00 amounts result from a £6.00 loyalty discount on the first order, and both charges are valid.
caveats: Timezone discrepancy: the transaction record shows 2025-04-12T08:11:33Z, while invoice A shows capture at 08:11:33 BST, which is 07:11:33 UTC. Confirm against acquirer authorisation logs that auth codes 442189 and 552781 match the two charges on this card, and that the invoice timestamp label is simply mislabelled.
Confirm that the second charge (auth 552781, 19:42) actually posted to the same card, and that neither charge has already been refunded or disputed separately.
Delivery confirmations are merchant-recorded on the invoices. DPD proof-of-delivery for both tracking numbers would strengthen the file but is not required under this rule.
The note on invoice B ('Both charges are valid') is merchant commentary, not evidence. It should not be relied on in the filing.
Both orders ship to the billing address, and AVS, CVV and 3DS results are clean. That is consistent with the cardholder placing both orders and misreading the equal amounts as a duplicate.

rule_text:
Visa 12.6.1 - Duplicate Processing
Issuer claim: The same transaction was processed more than once.
Logic: ALL 3 requirements must be satisfied.
Compelling evidence requirements:
  1. Evidence the two transactions are for two separate purchases (e.g. different order IDs, different items, different services rendered)
  2. Documentation of each purchase event (separate invoices, separate delivery confirmations, separate service dates)
  3. Transaction timestamps and authorisation codes for each charge
prechecks: AVS: Y (full address match); CVV: M (match); 3DS: frictionless
Chargeback raised 18 days after the transaction
